design_summary.purpose: Firmware-visible active-aerodynamics controller for 20–55 m/s operation that programs operating bounds, transports model requests and responses using the mandated direction contract, evaluates a physics-based surrogate against a transparent reference, enforces safety and freshness policies, and emits bounded actuator commands only when validated.
design_summary.operating_model: The top module is the synthesizable integration point for MMIO/CSR control, streaming model transport, surrogate/reference evaluation, safety bounding, timeout and stale-data tracking, and memory-backed history/payload storage. Firmware configures enable, surrogate selection, mode, timeout, stale limit, command bounds, and storage bases via MMIO; the datapath then packages request payloads, consumes response payloads, validates them, and either produces bounded actuator commands or deasserts validity and latches faults on invalid, stale, timeout, reset, or fault conditions. No fallback command or substitute controller is generated.

external_interfaces.name: MMIO/CSR control plane
external_interfaces.intent: Firmware-visible command/status interface with address, write-data, read-data, valid, write-enable, ready, and error semantics.

external_interfaces.name: External model transport
external_interfaces.intent: Mandated request/response direction contract: the RTL emits request valid/data, receives request ready, receives response valid/data, and emits response ready.

external_interfaces.name: Actuator command and status outputs
external_interfaces.intent: Final bounded actuator command outputs and firmware-visible fault/status reporting.

external_interfaces.name: Clock and reset
external_interfaces.intent: Global synchronous clocking with active-low reset fanout.

module_architecture.name: adaptive_aero_control_top
module_architecture.role: Firmware-controlled top-level controller integrating MMIO/CSR, streaming model transport, surrogate/reference evaluation, safety monitoring, timeout/staleness tracking, bounded actuator command generation, and memory-mapped bulk storage control.
responsibilities: Expose a real firmware-visible CSR/MMIO interface with address, write-data, read-data, valid, write-enable, ready, and error semantics.
Implement register decode for all declared software-visible registers and fields in DIGITAL_SPEC_JSON.register_contract.
Package and emit model-request transport traffic and capture model-response traffic using the mandated direction contract.
Evaluate transparent reference and physics-based surrogate outputs and compare them under bounded operating conditions.
Track stale-data age, model-response timeout, and control-loop fault conditions.
Generate bounded actuator commands only when validated; otherwise deassert validity and latch faults.
Provide MMIO access to bulk history/payload storage through technology-neutral memory wrappers.
Never create fallback commands or substitute controllers on fault conditions.
interface_notes: Top-level ports are fully described by the spec and must remain unchanged.
The top-level output ports are driven by the architectural partitions identified in the hierarchy, not by child-input-only connections.
MMIO-visible status and fault semantics are sourced from the safety and transport partitions and reflected through the CSR block.
ownership_notes: The top module owns the integration contract and is the required synthesizable design top.
It does not rename or redefine any child module, port, or filename.
It is the single point that ties firmware control-plane semantics to streaming transport and bounded actuation.

module_architecture.name: adaptive_aero_mmio_csr
module_architecture.role: Firmware-visible CSR/MMIO decode block that implements the complete control plane, status readback, fault latch clear semantics, configuration fields, and address decoding for the controller and memory windows.
responsibilities: Expose firmware-readable and firmware-writable configuration fields.
Provide explicit semantic outputs that other modules can consume without hidden derivation.
Bridge MMIO transaction semantics into controller configuration and storage address windows.
Reflect controller status and latched fault visibility to firmware.
interface_notes: Consumes MMIO address/write-data/valid/write-enable plus status inputs from controller partitions.
Drives configuration outputs for enable, surrogate selection, timeout, stale limit, actuator bounds, mode select, fault clear, and memory base fields.
Returns readback data and ready/error semantics through the MMIO port set.
ownership_notes: Owns the complete decode and readback behavior for the register contract.
All firmware-visible registers listed in the contract must be reachable through its decode logic.
It is the control-plane entry point and cannot be replaced by streaming transport.

module_architecture.name: adaptive_aero_transport
module_architecture.role: Streaming transport engine that packs request payloads for the physics-based surrogate, accepts response payloads, and exposes handshake status to the rest of the controller.
responsibilities: Emit model-request valid/data outputs and receive model-request ready as input.
Receive model-response valid/data inputs and emit model-response ready as output.
Stage request payload fields from controller-prepared semantic inputs.
Capture response payloads for validation and diagnostic use.
Expose transport-busy and transport-valid indicators to the controller.
Detect response staleness relative to the configured timing policy.
interface_notes: Uses the mandated external model transport direction contract exactly as specified.
The request path produces valid/data only from explicit semantic pack inputs and control state.
The response path consumes valid/data inputs and never drives request-side transport outputs.
ownership_notes: Owns the streaming transport protocol behavior only.
It does not implement actuator output generation or safety substitution.
It may coexist with MMIO but cannot replace it.

module_architecture.name: adaptive_aero_surrogate_reference
module_architecture.role: Physics-based surrogate and transparent reference evaluator that compares NVIDIA DoMINO-style surrogate outputs against a transparent reference model, computes validation metrics, and flags out-of-envelope or inconsistent predictions.
responsibilities: Evaluate the surrogate and reference outputs for active-aerodynamic control.
Provide explicit surrogate and reference command candidates for downstream comparison.
Flag invalid, stale, or out-of-envelope responses through validation outputs.
Respect configured actuator bounds and operating mode selection.
Keep the transparent reference separate from any bypass or fallback path.
interface_notes: Consumes response payloads and freshness indication from the transport block.
Produces packed state fields for request formation along with surrogate and reference command candidates.
Produces validation_valid, validation_error, and validation_delta_code for safety enforcement.
ownership_notes: This is the transparent reference partition and physics-based surrogate evaluation partition.
It is explicitly not a fallback controller.
It preserves distinct surrogate and reference command semantics for downstream safety decisions.

module_architecture.name: adaptive_aero_safety_bounding
module_architecture.role: Safety envelope and actuator command bounding stage that clamps accepted commands to configured limits, inhibits validity on invalid or stale conditions, and latches fault indicators for firmware handling.
responsibilities: Bound actuator outputs to configured tilt and deflection limits.
Deassert actuator validity on invalid, stale, timeout, reset, or fault conditions.
Latch faults until firmware clears them through the explicit clear-fault semantic.
Provide status and fault outputs to the MMIO block for software observation.
Never substitute a fallback command or alternate controller output.
interface_notes: Consumes validation results and candidate commands from the surrogate/reference evaluator.
Drives the final actuator command outputs, fault latch, and status outputs visible at the top level.
Reflects timeout/stale conditions as status indicators rather than replacing commands.
ownership_notes: Owns the final actuation gate and the fault-latching behavior.
It may retain internal safe state, but it must not assert validity without a fresh accepted command.

module_architecture.name: adaptive_aero_history_store
module_architecture.role: Technology-neutral bulk storage controller for control history and payload snapshots, intended to be mapped by the FPGA flow to native block RAM through declared memory macros.
responsibilities: Expose read data to firmware-facing logic and controller analytics.
Maintain technology-neutral memory mapping suitable for FPGA block RAM inference or binding.
Report simple busy indicators to prevent unsafe concurrent access.
Implement bulk storage as an inferred memory rather than a flattened bank of scalar registers.
Return stored read data through the declared functional output port.
interface_notes: Consumes only clock, reset, and firmware-configured base selectors.
Provides busy indicators for history and payload access sequencing.
Its bulk storage contract is explicitly memory-wrapper-based, not flattened into register arrays.
ownership_notes: Owns bulk history/payload storage control only.
It is technology-neutral and intended to map to inferred block RAM.
It does not affect actuator safety policy or model transport direction.

interface_summary.intent: Firmware issues MMIO transactions into the CSR decode block.
CSR block returns read data and transaction response semantics to firmware.
Transport block consumes request-ready and response-valid/data under the mandated direction contract.
Transport block emits request valid/data and response ready using the required handshake direction.
Firmware enable and surrogate-selection control the transport/request staging behavior.
Firmware configuration shapes surrogate/reference evaluation and operating envelope limits.
Firmware enable, clear-fault semantics, and output bounds control the final safety gate.
Firmware selects memory windows for bulk history and payload storage.
Evaluator provides packed semantic request fields for model-request formation.
Transport forwards response payload and freshness state for validation and reference comparison.
Evaluator presents candidate commands and validation outcomes to the final safety/bounding stage.
Safety stage drives the final bounded command and visible status/fault outputs.
Safety stage reports fault and timing status back to firmware through the CSR block.
Transport busy and model-valid indications are reflected into the firmware status readback path.
Safety status and response code are made visible through the MMIO register contract.

data_flow_summary: Firmware programs control, timeout, stale limit, bounds, mode, and storage-base registers via MMIO.
The surrogate/reference evaluator prepares packed semantic request fields for the transport engine.
The transport engine emits model-request valid/data and consumes model-request ready; it consumes model-response valid/data and emits model-response ready.
The surrogate/reference evaluator compares the accepted response against a transparent reference and produces validation outcomes and command candidates.
The safety bounding stage clamps validated commands to configured limits and only asserts actuator validity when inputs remain valid and fresh.
On invalid, stale, timeout, reset, or fault conditions, actuator validity is deasserted and the fault is latched for software handling; no fallback command is synthesized.
Bulk history/payload storage is controlled through a technology-neutral memory wrapper intended for FPGA block RAM mapping.

clock_reset_summary.clocking: All modules are synchronous to clk.
clock_reset_summary.reset_behavior: reset_n is active-low and fans out to all synchronous submodules. Reset initializes handshake state, configuration outputs, transaction state, freshness counters, and actuator validity to safe idle conditions. The architecture deasserts actuator command validity and status_valid during reset, preserves the no-fallback rule, and only clears a fault latch through explicitly defined software-controlled semantics rather than by substituting a command.

integration_notes: The MMIO/CSR interface is real and firmware-visible; streaming transport does not replace it.
The external model transport direction contract is applied by data flow even where application-specific naming varies.
Top-level outputs must be driven by actual RTL sources and not tied only to child inputs.
Bulk payload and history storage are described as technology-neutral inferred memory suitable for block RAM mapping, not as flattened registers.
The architecture supports bounded control, stale-data detection, timeout handling, and safe fallback behavior by inhibiting validity and latching faults, not by command substitution.
The design summary reflects an active-aerodynamics controller intended for 20–55 m/s operation with transparent reference evaluation and NVIDIA DoMINO-style surrogate partitioning.
consistency_notes: No hierarchy, ports, or filenames may differ from digital_spec_json.
